# Communication status block

Human time is the scarcest resource. Leading with analysis, preamble, and options wastes it. The human needs to scan, decide, and unblock — not read through thinking to find the actionable bit.

Every response ends with a structured status block. Four sections in order: INFO, INPUTS NEEDED, DONE, NEXT. The body of the response is work output. The status block is the executive summary.

- Every response MUST end with a status block (no session footer after it)
- Four sections in this order: INFO, INPUTS NEEDED, DONE, NEXT
- INFO: things affecting progress or decisions — blockers, risks, considerations
- INPUTS NEEDED: what decisions or actions the human must provide to unblock
- DONE: what was accomplished this turn
- NEXT: what the agent proposes to do next
- Skip any section that has nothing to report
- Keep each section to 1-3 bullet points max
- Do NOT front-load analysis and options before doing work
- Do the work first, show output, then give the status block
- Skip the status block for short exchanges (questions, confirmations, quick reads)
- Cockpit sessions (eagle-peak) use status blocks only after significant work, not every reply

## Scope

universal

## Consequences

- Human can scan the last few lines to know everything they need
- Decisions are concentrated, not scattered through prose
- Agent bias toward action over discussion
